title: new VR sculpt-and-film app — Build phase with smooth clay, doodles, layers and grab-to-scale yourself
notes: new VR sculpt-and-film app — Build phase with smooth clay, doodles, layers and grab-to-scale yourself

title: Shoot and Edit work — your right hand films takes with a 3-2-1, paths smooth and re-aim, the timeline trims them into an MP4. Plus blocks, skies with no ground, and finer layers
notes: Shoot and Edit work — your right hand films takes with a 3-2-1, paths smooth and re-aim, the timeline trims them into an MP4. Plus blocks, skies with no ground, and finer layers

title: Cast and Perform are in — make a starter puppet, step inside it, and record moves and your voice. Blocks can be picked up one by one and drawn as 4-point boxes at any angle
notes: Cast and Perform are in — make a starter puppet, step inside it, and record moves and your voice. Blocks can be picked up one by one and drawn as 4-point boxes at any angle

title: Cast is now Characters, its own studio where you sculpt puppets and props at your own size; Perform only grabs characters, never the scenery; pull windows off your hand with the grip
notes: CHARACTERS: a separate stage (yellow disc, no world) with its own saved view and scale. Make a puppet (head + two hands) or a prop (one piece), pick which part to sculpt, add extra parts.
PERFORM: place / bring characters in front of you, grab them with right grip (the ground can't be grabbed any more), step into puppets at their size, record moves and voice.

Windows: menu, Layers/Parts and the camera preview can be pulled out with right grip and left in the room, or docked back by bringing your hands together. Layers is its own window (right side on desktop).
Characters stand on the ground when placed. v0.3 scenes load: puppets become characters and the ground is put back where it belongs.

title: things no longer vanish when you're giant; 11 doodle brushes you can erase in bits, move and recolor; tear any tab off as its own window; teleport in Perform
notes: Fixed: when you scaled up, your hands, tools, windows and clay disappeared up close. The headset camera is now worked out at 1x and scaled, so nothing gets cut near your face at any size. Fog also scales with you.
A flips inside the tab you're on: Sculpt add/carve, Doodle draw/erase, Blocks build/erase. It never jumps to clay from Doodle or Blocks.
Doodle: Tube, Ribbon, Neon, Coil, Chain, Beads, Cubes, Dashes, Fuzz, Stars, Confetti. The eraser removes only the part it touches. Right grip moves a doodle, and Paint recolors doodles and blocks.
Grabbing uses the brush sphere at the tool tip instead of the middle of the controller.
Layers: Rename (keyboard in VR), Finer/Coarser any time (the clay is rebuilt, with a warning if it gets huge), and "Make it a prop".
Characters: a see-through Quest headset and controllers show where your head and hands go. Stepping in puts your eyes and hands there, facing the puppet's front. The studio has a floor grid.

Perform: right trigger aims at the ground and jumps you there. The countdown beeps. The selected take's camera and its view window show while you perform. Stick resizes the character you hold, and there's a size slider. Tap a motion row to play it.

Windows: grip a tab's content to tear it off. Right stick resizes a held window. The camera window docks at the bottom right of the menu. Squeezing both grips cancels a window grab so you move yourself.
Controller buttons are painted to match their labels. Color: hue / vivid / light sliders, colors you've used lately, and a 3D color ball you reach into.
4-point boxes update in place, so the preview no longer flickers.

title: new LIGHT phase with colored lights, materials and sun; APP phase for files and settings; pick your camera shot while you perform
notes: LIGHT: up to 6 colored lights (A adds one at your hand, grip a bulb to move it; color, brightness, reach). Materials per layer or character part: Clay, Plastic, Glossy, Metal, Chrome, Glow (+ Shiny / Metal / Glow sliders). Sun: brightness, height, direction, fill light, color.

APP on the phase dial: Files (save, download, load, new island, new empty sky) and Settings (fly speed, controller labels, countdown beeps, back to 1x, dock windows, color picker style). The Scene tab is gone from the other phases. APP keeps you where you were (world or studio).
PERFORM: "Camera shot" row: step through your takes with the arrows to choose which camera the window and the camera in the scene show, or tap + New shot to film another one in SHOOT.
Props start empty so you sculpt them from scratch. "Prop from layer" in CHARACTERS turns a BUILD layer into a prop.
Controller buttons keep getting repainted to match their labels (grab = purple, trigger = orange, stick = teal, A green, B red, X blue, Y yellow), even if the model reloads.
Color in the headset: a flat see-through Wheel with a light bar (default), a sparser Ball of dots, or Chips.

title: Scenes with their own timelines; your view rides along when you step into a puppet that already moves; stretch held things with two hands; voices and beeps fixed
notes: Scenes: PERFORM has a Scene row (◀ ▶, + Scene, tap the name to rename). Each scene is its own timeline of moves and voices, and takes belong to the scene they film. EDIT cuts shots from any scene together.
Step into a puppet whose moves you already recorded and your view follows those moves (smoothed), so you can act the gestures on top.
Two hands: hold a character (or a window) with the right grip and add the left grip to stretch and turn it. Right stick turns (↔) and sizes (↕) a held character. The size slider is gone.
Bring here / Place puts the character just in front of you at your feet.
Puppets get a body that hangs under the head and turns with you. "Clear" empties the part you're sculpting.

Sound: the audio engine starts on a real tap or click, so recorded voices and the countdown beeps play in the headset. Mic boost is in Settings. Voices show a waveform, and deleting one stops it right away. Tapping a Motion row draws its path.

SHOOT: square by default, and wide or vertical show more instead of cropping. "Smoothing for new takes" (0 keeps the shake). B deletes the key dot you're holding. Faster zoom on stick ↕, lens steps on ↔. The trigger films even while you point at the camera window.
Pop out (bottom of the menu rail) opens the tab you're on as its own window next to the menu, so Characters, Sculpt and Color can all be open at once.
Sculpt: new Spray tool. Doodles can be bent: "Right grip on a doodle → Bends it".

APP > Files: several worlds saved on this device (+ Island world / + Empty world, tap to open, tap the open one to rename). An update button appears when a newer version is online, and the version shows under the menu chip.
Controller buttons are painted in flat, unlit colors to match the labels. Settings shows how many it found on each controller.

title: export MP4s with voices (in the headset too, with cancel); zoom records while filming; voice effects and voice-only takes; stretch clips past the camera; tilt-shift
notes: Zoom you do while filming a take is now recorded with it.
EDIT: clips can end after the camera stopped (the camera holds still) so the action can finish. The timeline zooms (− / +). Dragging Start or End shows the exact frame you're cutting at.
Voices: tap a voice in Motion to set its volume, when it starts, and an effect (Plain, Echo, Robot, Radio, Cave), then hear it. "🎤 Voice only" in PERFORM records just your voice while the show plays.
Export: voices are mixed into the MP4. Works in the headset too (tap twice to confirm, progress bar, Cancel). When it's done, exit VR and tap the green Save MP4 button.
PERFORM: one character row with ◀ ▶, plus a new "On stage" tab listing every puppet and prop with Place / Bring here / Step in.
BUILD Layers window lists puppets and props too: eye shows or hides them in the scene, ✎ opens them in CHARACTERS. Scroll arrows when the list is long.
Stepping into a puppet now matches its eye height to your real eye height, so it feels the same at any size.
Lens: tilt-shift (shift up/down, left/right) and "Keep verticals straight". The stick ↔ lens steps are gone.
SHOOT has a Perform button to jump back.

title: grouped Layers window where you can move and lock layers and make set pieces that animate; trigger duplicates what you hold; letters on the controller buttons; puppet hands fixed
notes: Layers window is grouped into Set, Moving set, Props and Characters. Tapping a layer flashes it. Props and characters can be locked (no grabbing) and hidden. ✥ Move grabs the picked layer with your brush sphere, add the left grip to stretch it. In CHARACTERS: Center it, and Guides on/off.
"Animates" on a BUILD layer (a cloud, a wave) makes it a moving set piece you grab and record in PERFORM, still grouped with the set.
While holding a block or doodle, pull the trigger to leave a copy (like Gravity Sketch).
Grabbing is by touch: windows need your hand near them, and if your left grip is already squeezed, the right grip moves or sizes you instead of grabbing things.
The real A, B, X and Y buttons show their letters.
The color wheel stays above the menu the whole time you sculpt, doodle or build. Color has "Random each stroke".
New Slide doodle (a half-tube).
Puppet left and right hands were swapped; now fixed, and older puppets are fixed when they load. A guide hides when you hide its part.
New scenes can be made from SHOOT too (scene row on Takes).
PERFORM's window shows the camera by default. Mirror is off until you turn it on.
Voice editor: only the voice you're editing shows, with a Close button.

title: doodles can wave and spin, puppets get eyes and mouths that talk, and B deletes what you hold.
notes: Doodle moves page: Still / Wave / Spin (or Twist, Pulse) with speed and power sliders; saved with the world and in exports
Slide doodle is smooth and has real thickness, rims and end caps
Holding a block or doodle: B deletes it, both grips stretch and turn it
Letters sit on the face of each A/B/X/Y button
New puppets start empty; + Eye, + Mouth and Copy eye in Characters
Eyes look at you, or where you steer them with the right stick while stepped in (recorded)
Mouths open with your voice while stepped in or on Voice only (recorded)
Colour wheel sits below your hand and the yellow line can pick from it; Settings: below / above / off

title: play together. Host a room with a 4-digit code, sculpt side by side, and hand her a puppet to play. Voices get a pitch slider.
notes: APP → Together: Host a room, or type a code to join (Quest 3 to Quest 3)
The host runs every menu; a player gets Sculpt, Color, Doodle and Blocks with their own color and size
Players ride along at the host's size and place; "Line up next to me" puts them a step to your right
You see each other's headset and Touch Plus controllers
Perform: "Put Player 2 in <puppet>" hands it over; their head, hands, eyes and mouth record into your takes
Their voice records on its own track whenever you record
Clay, doodles, blocks, layers, characters, sky and lights stay in sync; undo works for both
Voice editor: Pitch slider (±12 notes) that keeps the timing

title: camera takes now run until the last puppet move or voice, and the Motion list scrolls.
notes: A take holds its last camera spot until everything recorded in its scene has finished, and keeps up as you record more
Dragging a clip's End in EDIT sets it by hand; "End follows the puppets & voices" turns following back on
Motion tab: ▲ ▼ buttons and a draggable bar when there are more rows than fit

title: edit doodles after drawing (hold one + A), puppets stay where you let go, and the studio guides are your real controllers.
notes: Hold a doodle + A: Edit doodle page (brush type, thickness, color, moves, yellow points to bend, delete)
Letting go of a character or prop mid-take keeps it there; trigger while holding lets you re-grip
Studio guides show the actual Touch Plus controllers at the exact pose your hands take when you step in
Puppet body turns with your hands and head together, so the head can shake "no" on its own
Your own head, eyes and mouth no longer sit in front of your eyes when stepped in
Settings: "Turn any way" (no fixed ground, also when stepping in) or "Ground stays down"
Sculpt size slider covers exactly the sizes the brush can make; strength stays full; right stick ← → switches Sculpt / Doodle / Blocks
Camera view drawn like a Blender camera in SHOOT and EDIT
Lights keep the same reach in the scene however big you are
New Audio tab under Motion; each character can have its own voice effect and pitch for new takes
Doodles: Confetti is now Balls, and a new Confetti of tumbling squares; Slide no longer glitches at its ends when animated
Studio is lit from the front

title: the sky is back, and joining a room with a big world no longer kicks the player out.
notes: v0.13 stopped drawing the sky and fog outside the character studio (all black); fixed
PeerJS closes the connection on any message of 16 KB or more; everything now goes in small paced pieces
The player sees "Getting the world… %" while it loads, and a dropped connection while loading retries by itself
A refused message no longer counts as someone leaving

title: film your partner live while she plays a puppet, save worlds to GitHub for every device, and new brushes and block shapes.
notes: SHOOT: she stays in her puppet; your camera take records her moves and voice
Perform tab lists each player with put in / take out
Together: slide, raise and turn her headset, or grab it with your grip; her menu shows on her controller
Other people's headsets never show up in your shots
Fixed puppet hands that stopped following when the controllers woke up in swapped slots
Voices: louder and gently compressed, mic turns on when you step in, CHARACTERS > Voice tab with "Try it"
Camera hears the characters (EDIT > Export): closer and in view = louder, left/right pan, 0–200%
EDIT: several cuts of the same takes
☁ GitHub button: Save to GitHub / From GitHub in Files; MP4s can go there too
Blocks: Box, Ball, Tube, Cone, Pyramid, Donut
Doodles: Flames, Snow, Crystal, Black holes
Color wheel: hold the trigger and push in for darker, pull out for lighter
Color tab moved to the bottom; character page pages through many parts

title: recordings stay in sync, undo only takes back your own work, and eyes, mouths and hands behave.
notes: Recording and playback follow the real clock, so a slow moment no longer puts puppets out of step with each other
Together: undo only takes back what you did; the host can undo / redo for a player from Together
A copied eye or any new part always shows up on the other headset
Eyes look relative to the head however you turned them; mouths open gently and never pile up or fly off
A puppet hand works even if that controller was asleep when you stepped in (and tells you to wake it)
Voices: much lighter squeeze, each one evened out in loudness
Picking a color turns Random off; a dot shows where you point on the color wheel, in that color
Doodle moves are off by default and 20 times gentler
Doodle brush tip is a pen nib; block ghost shows the chosen form
The rail fits every tab (Color was under Pop out)
New characters get silly names

title: voice effects with sliders, hear yourself live, 10 songs, puppet arms, a body diagram, and puppets can grab, climb and eat props
notes: Voice effects: Echo (delay, feedback, wet), Robot, Radio, Cave and Squeeze (threshold, ratio, attack, release), each on/off with its own sliders, in the Voice tab and on every recorded clip
Mic records clean now (no more 2.5x boost), which was the main cause of the crunch
"Hear me" in Perform and "Hear myself live" in Voice: your mic with the puppet's pitch and effects, even when not recording
Music: 10 built-in songs per scene with speed and volume; plays with the show, takes, film and export
Characters: tap the head, eyes, mouth, body or hands on a drawing to sculpt that part (List view still there); arms as String, Elbow or Bellows with thickness, color and "Set shoulders"
Other worlds: bring characters in from your other worlds on this headset
As a puppet: grip near a prop to hold it (it records), grip on doodles or blocks to move them, grip on nothing to climb; bring food to your mouth to eat it (X undoes)

title: a big editor where takes stack on lanes so you can cut and swap between them, with audio lanes, and editing, roaming and filming together
notes: Edit: new takes of the same scene stack on parallel lanes, lined up in show time. Tap a lane and "Show from here" (or tap a lane while the film plays) to switch to it; "Cut here" splits a clip at the playhead; trim, move or drop clips and lanes
Audio lanes for each character's voice, other sounds and music, each with mute and volume per cut, used in playback and the MP4
The big editor is its own wide window under the film screen in the headset, and along the bottom on desktop; the menu has a smaller copy
Together: the edit, the film screen and play/stop show for the other player too
A player can move and size herself on her own ("Bring back" on the host's Together page), and pick her own layer to sculpt on
Doodles show up for the other player while they are being drawn
"Give her the camera": the player films with her trigger while you act in a puppet, in the same take

title: smooth or lighten a whole clay layer, pick parts on a body drawing in the Layers window, and redo just part of a performance
notes: Layers window: "Smooth all" smooths the whole layer and keeps skinny bits; "Lighten" keeps the look with about a quarter of the triangles in one draw, goes back to full detail while you sculpt, and lightens again after
Characters: the parts drawing is now in the Layers window (Drawing or List), plain until you pick a part, which lights up yellow
Puppets start with one eye; repeated parts are numbered in the list
Mirror a hand to the other side; set where an eye turns or a mouth opens from with the brush (pink dot), or keep it automatic
Each character shows how heavy it is (aim under 150k triangles)
Color: a dice for random colors next to the floating picker, a wider light bar, and a new Sliders picker (hue, saturation, value); the Color page uses hue, saturation and value too
Perform: tap the show timeline to pick a spot; Record then redoes from there and keeps what comes before and after
Characters blink when you cycle to them in Perform
Arm tubes face the right way; climbing with grips is off unless you turn it on
Real controllers hide inside a puppet's sculpted hands
Faster: hidden windows are not redrawn, and the camera preview renders at half rate unless the film plays

title: a switcher grid that shows every take at once, a sharper film screen, drag lanes to the top, tap sounds to change their effects, and a longer, steadier zoom
notes: Edit: "Grid" shows every take of the moment under the playhead side by side; point and pull the trigger (or click) to cut to one, even while it plays; the red frame is the one showing
The film screen in the headset renders sharper (1280 wide), and windows like the editor no longer show up inside shots or the MP4
Drag a lane name up or down; the top lane shows for the whole clip
Up to 12 takes stack in one clip (the 7th no longer starts a new clip)
Tap a voice or music block in the audio lanes to change its pitch, effects and volume in the menu, or copy them to all of that character's lines
Zoom goes to about 12x; the closer you zoom, the more the camera is steadied, live and in the take
Desktop: the film view no longer hides behind the editor; the menu redraws less often while things play

title: a simple hand menu in Edit, a smooth compact take grid, sound settings in the editor, and a screen that stays where you put it
notes: Hand menu in Edit is just Play, Cut, Grid, Dark room, Stack takes, cuts and the Export tab; the timeline lives in the big editor
The film screen renders every frame again (the every-other-frame trick made one eye flash) and stays put and sized when you press play or toggle the grid
Grid: tiles pack as big as they fit on a wide screen (six vertical takes sit in one row); every tile updates every frame, with "Grid: lighter while it plays" as an option
Lanes have up/down arrows as well as dragging; the top lane shows for the whole clip
Tap a character's sound lane name to set that voice for all its lines: lane volume, pitch and every effect, right in the big editor; tap one sound block to change just that line
"Sound from this take": a clip keeps the close-up take's sound even when you cut to a far shot
No camera pyramid floating around in Edit

title: puppet arms move in exported videos
notes: puppet arms move in exported videos

title: the left-hand menu always comes back
notes: The menu re-attaches itself to whichever controller is your left one right now, so it can't stay stuck on a controller that went to sleep or swapped
With no left controller, the menu waits in front of you and goes back on your hand when it returns
If the film preview ever fails, the windows (menu included) can no longer stay hidden
Hiding the menu with the left trigger now says how to bring it back

title: the hand menu can't be hidden inside things, and holding the left trigger brings it in front of you
notes: The left-hand menu draws on top of everything, so a puppet's hand, clay or the mirror can't swallow it
Hold the left trigger for a second: the menu jumps in front of you (grab it back to your left hand any time)
The pointer dot and the color picker still show in front of the menu

title: audio lanes in Edit show waveforms
notes: audio lanes in Edit show waveforms

title: the hand menu is back in Shoot, Perform and Edit, the pointer shows again, and you grab windows by pointing
notes: Fixed since v0.19: drawing the camera picture each frame left the hand menu (and Layers and camera windows) switched off in Shoot, Perform and Edit
The pointer ray and dot show in front of the menu again (v0.23's draw-on-top menu covered them)
In Edit the ray reaches the film screen, so you can see which grid tile you're pointing at
Point at any window or the film screen and grip to move it (no need to touch it); the right stick resizes while holding; windows answer from up to 3 m
Big editor: buttons in two rows, larger, and larger lane names so they read in the headset
Older sounds without a character can be given one ("Whose voice?"), so each character gets its own audio lane

title: new doodle brushes (playground tube with windows, picket, chain link and barbed wire fences, Victorian trim, rocks, rainbow), and slides always open to the sky
notes: Slide: the open half always faces up, and it is as wide as the brush (old slides keep their look)
Tube is now a crawl-through playground tube, as wide as the brush, with thick walls you can see from inside and see-through windows every so often
The old thin tube is now called Doodle
Picket (white), Chain link and Victorian trim hang down from the line you draw; Barbed wire twists with spikes; Rocks scatter stones of different shapes; Rainbow draws seven stripes
Doodle thickness goes bigger (up to about 24 cm across)

title: a stroke keeps drawing when your hand passes over the menu or the color picker
notes: a stroke keeps drawing when your hand passes over the menu or the color picker

title: playground tubes and slides stay round and smooth, and rocks are solid
notes: Tube and slide follow the gist of your hand instead of every wobble, so they no longer pinch into sausages
Their cross-section is carried along the line and can't flip: tubes never twist on themselves, and slides turn gently to open upward
Rocks no longer have cracks that made them look half see-through

title: pose first, so puppet hands sit in your grip the way you'll actually perform
notes: Characters: "Pose my hands" counts down 3 s while you stand how you'll act; the see-through controller guides move and tilt to exactly where your hands were, so you sculpt the hands around them
Hands you already sculpted move with the new pose, keeping their place around your grip (X undoes)
Stepping into the puppet uses those recorded hand angles, so the hands look the same when you perform as when you sculpted them
"Try it on" jumps straight into the puppet in Perform to check it

title: place a puppet right where you stand at your size, a brush that keeps shrinking, and pictures of characters from other worlds
notes: Placing a puppet in the headset puts it exactly around you, facing your way and sized to you, as if you were already inside it
Shrinking your clay brush past a layer's detail makes that layer finer by itself (when it stays light), and the cursor shows the real brush size
Characters from your other worlds show a little picture of each one before you add it, four to a page

title: a new scene starts with everyone exactly where the last scene ended
notes: a new scene starts with everyone exactly where the last scene ended

title: stepping into a puppet you moved from outside keeps its body on that motion, and re-recording overwrites instead of stacking
notes: Motion list grouped by character (header per character, clear-all per character)
Step into a puppet that has whole-character motion: body stays locked to it, head and hands act relative to it, view stays level
Re-recording replaces only the overlapping time, for motion and for that character's voice
A take that starts mid-timeline holds its first pose before it
Layer eye has a third state: only in the movie (hidden while you work, shown in the MP4)
Layer detail cycles Full / Lighter / Rough (rough while you work, full detail in the MP4)
Shoot's Takes page shows the show timeline; tap it to look at a moment

title: version numbers now count your ideas; this build is about idea #380
notes: version numbers now count your ideas; this build is about idea #380

title: the camera's preview screen is twice as big and sits on its back; hold grip and use the stick to move it, A and B to size it
notes: Screen centered on the back of the camera, facing you, at double the old size
Right grip held in Shoot: stick moves the screen, A makes it bigger, B smaller (zoom and take buttons pause while you hold grip)
Controller labels switch to the screen controls while you hold grip
Screen position and size are remembered

title: Perform and Shoot are now one ACTION phase, and the camera films from wherever you set the timeline
notes: ACTION rail: Puppets, On stage, Motion, Audio, Camera, Path, Keys, Lens. Camera tabs make your right hand the camera; the others work the puppets
Tap the timeline in Camera to look at that moment; filming starts there
Left trigger brings a floating menu back to your hand; touching the menu to your left hand docks it too; holding the trigger no longer floats it
Right grip in the Camera tabs: left stick moves the camera's screen, right stick sizes it
The floating camera window stays off in the headset while filming, and never hides behind the scene when it is on
Camera path and keyframe dots only show on the Path and Keys tabs

title: step into a tilted or lying-down puppet and its down becomes your down, so standing straight keeps it straight on its side
notes: Stepping in works out the puppet as if it stood upright, then tips you with it
Your head and hands move in the puppet's own frame; its body stays where you left it
Your view stays level while your eyes ride in its head

title: focus blur for the camera, a marker over the puppet you pick, Voices and Music tabs, and the puppet tools in their own panel
notes: ACTION: a bouncing marker (seen through walls) and a flash show which character you picked in On stage or Puppets
ACTION rail trimmed to Puppets, On stage, Motion, Voices, Music, Camera, Lens (Path and Keys tabs gone)
Lens: lens shift is replaced by focus blur, per take, focusing on the middle of the frame or at a set distance; applies to the preview, Edit and the MP4
Voices and Music tabs each have play and a timeline you can tap
Music volume changes while it plays; a toggle picks whether faster music also sounds higher
Stepping in: only a lean over ~30° counts as tilted; your controllers show whenever the puppet's hand isn't on them
CHARACTERS: puppets only (props are layers that animate); the puppet tools and Voice are a panel on the right of the menu; the left trigger hides every panel on your hand

title: CHARACTERS menu is Puppet, Voice, Parts with the sculpt tools in a side panel, and a voice change reaches everything that character already said
notes: CHARACTERS menu rail: Puppet, Voice, Parts, Tools; Sculpt, Doodle, Blocks and Color sit in the Tools panel on the right
Changing a character's voice updates every take of theirs, in every scene
Voices: an open voice stays open until Close; its strip shows the sound with a playhead you tap or drag; "Hear it from here" plays from that spot and turns into Stop while it plays
Carrying a window near your left hand gives it a glowing border and a buzz: let go and it snaps back

title: All multiplayer apps: online play now connects across different wifi and phone data (new relay server)
notes: All multiplayer apps: online play now connects across different wifi and phone data (new relay server)

title: a "Seen only" lane in the Edit timeline mutes voices whose character is out of the camera's picture
notes: New lane under the video lanes: one switch per clip, pink = only hear characters inside the frame (walls ignored), with a quick fade
Tap the lane's name to switch every clip at once
"Camera hears the characters" (0–200%) moved from Export to the end of that lane
Works in Edit playback and in the MP4

title: voices that drifted out of sync can snap back to their puppets with one tap ("Line up")
notes: Voices tab: "Line up all voices with their mouths" slides each voice so its loudness matches the mouth motion recorded with it
In a voice: 🎯 Auto does the same for that one; ◀◀ .1 / ◀ .02 / .02 ▶ / .1 ▶▶ nudge it by hand, and you hear the change right away if it's playing
Undo (X) puts voices back
Multiplayer uses the shared turn-config.js relay instead of its own Open Relay login

title: Edit plays with B and records shot changes with A like Action, voices no longer go near-silent on far shots, and App has a list of every update
notes: Edit: B plays / stops the film; A plays and records lane taps as shot changes (tapping lanes during plain play no longer switches)
Camera hearing is gentler: far-away or off-center shots dip the voice instead of almost muting it
Timeline: each take shows a bright bar for the part of the scene it actually filmed; the rest is shaded
App → Updates: every version's notes, newest first, each change numbered from the first one

title: the Edit screen stays upright when you grab it, zooms with both grips, and the grid re-flows when you stretch its corner
notes: Grip the film screen: it follows your hand but stays level and turns to face you (no more twisting it upside down)
Hold the left grip too and spread or pinch your hands to zoom it
Grid view: grip near a corner and stretch; the takes re-arrange to fit (6 in a row, 3 x 2, 2 x 3...), and the shape is remembered

title: old worlds can split their "other sounds" into one audio lane per character with one tap
notes: Voices tab and Edit's "other sounds" panel: "🎭 Give voices to their characters" works out who said each old voice, by its name or by whose mouth moved with it, across every scene
Any voice: a "Who says it" picker (◀ ▶) to set or fix the character by hand
Once a voice has a character it gets that character's own lane in Edit

title: inside a puppet, gripping a wall climbs and gripping air does nothing; outside moves stay put when you step in; voices only replace each other from inside
notes: Grip a surface (clay, the ground, a block, a doodle) while in a puppet to climb; gripping empty air does nothing (no more being dragged around by your left hand)
A puppet you walked around from outside keeps that walk when you step in: climbing and jumping are off while you ride it, so its body motion is never overwritten
A new voice take only replaces that character's older voice when you recorded it stepped inside them; voice you add while puppeting from outside is kept alongside
Brushes that turn upright (rainbow, slide, fences, trim) now roll smoothly along the line instead of creasing or snapping, with no extra cost

title: A plays and B records everywhere, takes stay in order on the timeline, and cuts, the film's start and end, and a sound blend at cuts can all be dragged
notes: A = play / stop, B = record, in ACTION and EDIT (buttons and labels match)
Edit lanes stay in take order; the lit lane is the one showing. Tap a lane (or its name) to turn it on from that point; no more shuffling lanes to the top
Yellow handles on each switch inside a clip, and white handles where two clips join: drag them to slide the cut
Yellow brackets on the ruler set where the film starts and ends (per cut); playback and the MP4 use that range
"Cut blend" (0–2 s) on the Seen only row: the camera's sound (loudness, left/right, seen-only) glides across each cut instead of jumping
The MP4 now always includes the newest voices of the scene you're in

title: cut old "other sounds" into pieces, split by who was talking, and give each piece its own character lane or mute it; Files shows all your worlds
notes: Edit: tap a sound on its lane, then "✂ Split at the playhead" or "🎭 Split by who was talking" (uses whose mouth was moving)
Each piece can go to a character (it moves to their lane) or be muted with "🔈 Mute this piece"; works in playback and the MP4
App → Files: "All ▸" lists every world saved on this device, newest first, with dates; only the newest 4 show on the main page

title: Edit's sound lanes scroll when there are more than fit, and windows you carry stay upright
notes: When the sound lanes don't fit, a ▲ Up / ▼ Down row appears under them, and the right stick ↕ scrolls them in Edit
Any window you grab and carry (Editor, menu, panels) stays upright and turns to face you, tipped back a little for reading; it can no longer be twisted upside down

title: older worlds sort their voices into each character's own lane by themselves, and Edit can empty the timeline while keeping every puppet and voice
notes: Opening Edit or Action in a world with unlabeled voices now works out who said each one automatically: by name, by whose mouth moved with it, or by whose recorded motion started and ended with that recording
Voices whose character was deleted go to "Other sounds" instead of a nameless lane
"🧹 Empty the timeline" (Edit menu and the big editor): removes this cut's clips and their camera takes; puppets, their motion and all voices stay; new camera takes land on the empty timeline

title: "Voices back as recorded" rejoins chopped-up voices into whole takes, nothing ever deletes a voice now, and the editor drops its unused buttons
notes: "↩ Voices back as recorded" (Edit menu and Voices tab, tap twice): every voice that was split into slivers, trimmed, muted or piece-muted becomes one whole recording again, then gets sorted to its character
Re-recording inside a character silences an older take it fully covers instead of deleting it, so it can always be brought back
"Split by who was talking" is gone: it chopped full takes into slivers when every puppet's mouth was moving at once
Big editor buttons: Play, Record, Cut here, Drop clip, Grid, − zoom, + zoom (Show from here, Whole clip, Move, Sound from and Drop lane removed)

title: Edit works one scene at a time (◀ Scene ▶ like ACTION), and Export can string every scene together; a Show bar with scene, timeline, play and record sits above the menu on every ACTION tab
notes: Each scene has its own edit timeline and cuts; switching scenes in Edit or ACTION swaps to that scene's timeline
Older worlds with one shared timeline are split by scene automatically (nothing deleted)
Export: "Just this scene" or "Whole film: every scene in order" (each scene's chosen cut)
Editor title says which scene and cut you're editing
Show bar (transport controls): scene ◀ ▶, time, timeline, ⏮, Play (A), Record (B), Voice only / Film from here
Bring here moves a puppet's recorded walk along with it
On stage: red ✕ takes a puppet out of the scene (undoable)
Camera keyframe dots stay a steady size on screen

title: stepping in puts the puppet's hands right where you made them in Characters, and right grip grabs puppets from outside again, even ones with recorded moves
notes: Step in: head, hands and body now line up from the Characters pose. Before, they lined up from wherever an earlier take left them at time 0, so the offset grew with every take
Grab from outside: puppets with recorded moves can be grabbed; letting go carries the whole recorded walk so that moment lands where you put it
Touching a puppet wins over pointing at a window behind it, so the Show bar and menu don't steal the grab
Grab works on the ACTION camera tabs too; grip away from a puppet still adjusts the camera screen

title: tap a cut mark in the Edit timeline to remove it; the marks are thin now instead of thick yellow bars
notes: Cut marks inside a clip (where the shot switches takes) are a thin line with a small ✕ tab on top
Tap the tab: the cut is gone and the shot carries on with the take before it. Drag the tab to slide it like before
Tap the white join between two clips made with "Cut here": they become one clip again
X undoes either one

title: when your controllers rest and the headset swaps in bare hands, the app ignores the hands instead of glitching
notes: Bare-hand input from Quest's auto-switch is ignored: nothing gets stuck to your wrists, the menu and puppet parts stay put
Pick up a controller and it works again right away
A one-time hint points to the Quest setting that stops the auto-switch for good

title: 17 new hand-written songs, each a little scene, with a song list on the Music tab
notes: New songs: Snail Waltz in Seven, Picnic Three Against Two, Giant Steps Tiny Feet, Clockwork Round, Phase Garden, Moon of Seven, Forever Up the Stairs, Spilled Spaghetti Tarantella, Metric Mischief, Gamelan Gumdrops, Rainy Bus Stop Bossa, Mirror Twins, Octatonic Ostrich, Five Lanterns, Goblin Market Hocket, Goodbye Little Robot, Brave Little Hero

Rhythm: 7/8, 12/8 bell pattern with hemiola, 5/4 with a shaker in 4 against 5, 9/8 + 11/8, metric modulation, Reich-style phasing, euclidean drums, a Risset rhythm that speeds up forever, breathing gamelan tempo, rubato

Harmony: Coltrane changes, Neapolitan and augmented sixths, Picardy third, line cliché and tritone subs, negative-harmony mirror, octatonic minor-third sequence, quartal chords, just intonation with the 7th harmonic, Shepard tones
New little orchestra: FM bells, mallets, kalimba, gamelan with shimmering paired tuning, plucks, winds, brass, strings, real drum kit, reverb and echo; every song loops seamlessly
Music tab lists every song with the scene it fits; tap one to hear it under the scene. Old songs and saved worlds are unchanged

title: when you step into a puppet that already has a recorded walk and take a few steps, its body now follows you instead of leaving your head behind
notes: The body keeps its recorded walk plus a smoothed step toward where your head went (and a little toward your hands)
Recording from inside saves that adjusted walk, so the body stays under the head on replay
Stepping into a puppet you moved somewhere else from outside still puts your head right in its head

title: "♪ Snap" makes the timeline snap to the music's beats; in Edit, tap a take to switch to it at the playhead, double-tap to cut right where you tap
notes: ♪ Snap button on the Show bar and in the Edit buttons: scrubbing, the Edit playhead, dragged cut marks and double-tap cuts land on the song's beats (faint yellow beat lines show where), using the scene's song at its speed
Fast songs snap to bigger steps (the tarantella to its dotted-quarter beat)
Edit lanes: one tap switches to that take from the playhead; double-tap cuts to it at the tapped spot; tapping a clip the playhead isn't in just moves the playhead there
Removed the note overlapping the Puppets title

title: puppets blink (click a stick when you're inside one), Extra parts like ears wobble a little, and a thirds grid for the camera screen
notes: Blink: inside a puppet, click either thumbstick to blink, hold it to keep the eyes shut; it records with the eyes. Puppets nobody is steering blink on their own every few seconds

Wobble: Extra parts (ears, antennae, tails, hats) swing gently from where they join the head when the puppet moves, then settle; it shows in the camera and in exported films, never in the recorded motion
Lens tab: "Thirds grid on the camera screen" draws rule-of-thirds lines on the camera's screen and the Edit screen (never in the film)
Controller labels show the new stick-click blink

title: your partner sees your camera picture and the edit, a magic eraser clears every layer at once, and stepping in sizes you to the puppet as it is right now
notes: Partner's screen: while you're on an ACTION camera tab, her preview window shows what your camera sees; in Edit it shows the film playing. It turns off when you leave, and when she holds the camera herself
Magic eraser (Sculpt page, or key 7 on desktop): one stroke carves clay and clears doodles and blocks on every visible, unlocked layer you're working in; one undo puts it all back
Step in: uses the puppet's real size at that moment (a recorded walk can have grown or shrunk it) and no longer caps how tall or tiny a puppet can be, so its arms match yours
Inside a puppet, only your head leads the body (with a small dead zone), so waving your hands no longer slides it around
Older saved layers without a saved pose can't break stepping in

title: step into puppets that are upside down, lying down or sideways without glitches; 1:1 size and a try-on mirror in Characters
notes: Tilted puppets: you tip with the puppet so its down is your down, and its head and hands sit exactly on your headset and controllers (before, hands could be up to a metre off and the view could flip)
Inside any puppet, its head, hands and face follow your real head and hands exactly; your view keeps up with a moving puppet more closely
Characters: "1:1 size" puts your eyes at the puppet's eye height, so your real reach is its reach and your hands fill its see-through controllers. Pose my hands switches to 1:1 by itself
Characters: "Try it on" now stays in Characters with a mirror; "Take it off" (or leaving Characters) steps out. No sculpting while you wear it

title: duplicate characters, eyes that follow a ✛ target you move and record, a "where it looks" arrow for each eye, plus doodle categories, a brick brush and colored stones
notes: Characters: ⧉ Duplicate makes a full copy (every part, its guides, voice and arms) you can change on its own or place as another of the same character; a placed one lands beside the first

ACTION · Puppets: "eyes follow a ✛ you move" shows a yellow cross; grab it with the right grip and the eyes aim at it. Moving it while recording puts it on the timeline; letting go when not recording leaves it there

Characters: pick an eye and use "Set where it looks ➜" (point your right controller, pull the trigger) to give it its own straight-ahead; a yellow arrow shows it. Every eye now aims from its own straight-ahead, so splayed eyes still look at the right thing
Blinking: stick click also blinks a puppet you're holding from outside, and works while trying one on
Doodle brushes sorted into Lines, Build, Bits and Magic; new Bricks brush (a little two-course wall under your line)
Bricks, Rocks, Picket, Chain link and Barbed can take your brush color instead of their own

title: stepping into a puppet that lies sideways somewhere in its walk now works, and doodle brush families have their own colors
notes: Step in reads the puppet's pose where you are on the timeline, so a puppet that is upright at the start but sideways now no longer throws your view 90° off and puts your eyes 1.5 m from its head
If it tips over during a take, you tip with it (past about 30°) and come back level once it stands up again; your view keeps up more closely while it falls
Doodle: Lines pink, Build orange, Bits teal, Magic violet, on the tabs and as a stripe on each brush

title: Inside a puppet, the grip now grabs while you hold it and lets go when you release it
notes: Inside a puppet, the grip now grabs while you hold it and lets go when you release it

notes: Eyes, mouths, extras and the new Hair part follow the head's recorded moves, so

notes: Together: the second player hears the show's music and voices when the host plays,

Stepped in: the body hangs from your neck instead of your eyes, so when you nod
Fixed the hair/extras sway using a wrong pivot when there was no head.

notes: Takes: every recording is a take, shown as a bright bar on the show timeline

notes: Re-recording: the voice of the character you're redoing (inside it, holding it,

Color: white and black circles next to the dice (on the 3D color ball and the

title: five new doodles (road, flowers, vines, floating water, tentacles) and one Wiggle slider that sways every doodle at once
notes: Road (Build): asphalt with white edges and a dashed yellow middle line, lies flat along your stroke.
Flowers (Bits): stems with petals in your brush color and yellow middles.
Vines (Bits): winding green stem with leaves and curly tendrils (can take your color).
Floating water (Magic): zero-gravity water blobs that jiggle and drift on their own.
Tentacle (Bits): thick to thin, any color, suction cups in the opposite color; it waves by itself.
Doodle moves page: "Every doodle at once" Wiggle + Speed. Doodles with their own moves keep them. Saved with the world and shared with your partner.
Knotted rope confirmed in the Lines list.

title: Sky patterns (clouds, twinkly stars, swirl, aurora, confetti), 8 clay finishes like glitter and pearl, outlines on puppets, and a face cam that rides on a puppet's head
notes: LIGHT now holds Sky, Sun, Lights and Materials together (Sky moved over from BUILD).
Sky & world: "Pattern in the sky" with Amount and Speed. Stars twinkle, clouds drift, all of it shows in films.
Materials: a Finish row on every layer: Sand, Glitter (sparkles as you move around it), Pearl, Velvet, Terrazzo, Marble, Lava (glows by itself).
CHARACTERS > Look: outline On/Off, Stroke or Glow, 4 thicknesses plus fine tune, color swatches or your brush color. Same width on screen near or far.

ACTION > Camera > Face cam: pick a puppet and the camera rides its head. Distance, around, height, steady, zoom, level horizon, or place it with your camera hand. It's a lane in Edit, so you can cut to it.

title: Export the film on your phone while it's joined to the headset, safer joins for big projects, and a Smaller file (HEVC) option
notes: Phone export: join the headset's room from the phone, go to EDIT > Export, tap "Export MP4 to this phone". It gets the latest film from the headset, says "Got everything, safe to turn off the headset", renders on the phone and saves it there (green Save MP4 button opens the share sheet).

Safe join: the world comes in numbered pieces. Pieces that arrive are kept, even if the connection drops; only missing ones are asked for again. Shows % and pieces while it loads, then "got everything".
The second player's timeline now updates whenever the host's recorded moves change.
Export: "Smaller file" uses HEVC (H.265) when the browser can, else a lighter H.264. Your fps (60 too) stays as picked. The file size shows when it's done.

title: Export for Blender: one zip with the 3D scene, every sound and a script that rebuilds the film in Blender
notes: EDIT > Export > "Export for Blender (.zip)".
scene.glb: sets, puppets and their parts with the recorded moves baked on every frame (eyes, mouths, dangling legs included), lights, and one camera per take, moving like in the film.
sounds/: full_mix.wav (like the MP4), music.wav, and one WAV per voice clip with its mutes and bleeps already in.

rebuild_in_blender.py: open it in Blender's Scripting tab and press Run. It loads the scene, sets fps, size and frame range, binds the camera cuts to timeline markers, keys each camera's zoom, makes the sky and sun, and lays every sound on the Video Sequencer at the right frame. Tested in Blender 5.3.
Puppet arms come in still at the first frame.

title: "Send everything to the phone" from the headset, the phone keeps the world when the headset turns off, and smoother playback
notes: Together (host): "📱 Send everything to the phone". The phone saves the whole world as its own world ("From the headset · date") and says when it's safe to turn off the headset; the headset shows "Phone has everything ✓".

Phone: when the headset goes off or sleeps, the phone stays in the world (saved, with the newest moves) instead of jumping back to its old one. Keep editing on the phone, or EDIT > Export renders right on the phone. It also notices a headset that just went dark (12 s).
Phone (Together): "Keep this world on this phone & leave". Plain Leave still goes back to your own world.

Playback: voice effects (echo, robot, cave) are now really switched off when sound stops; they used to keep running in the background and pile up every play and every cut, which made the sound glitch more and more.
Lines further than 2.5 s ahead are wired up just before they play, so only a few effect chains run at once.
Edit playback: switching lanes in one stretch no longer restarts the music, and voices cross over in 40 ms with no click.

Headset: while playing, the small preview screen draws every other frame and a playing grid redraws one lane per frame; no music composing in the background during playback; track sync to partners pauses while playing.

title: Talk to each other in the room, a light just on one puppet, a phone layout, and a better Blender export
notes: Together: everyone in the room now hears everyone live, built in (no more phone calls on the side). "🎙 Talking" mutes just your talk (your recordings keep the mic); "🔊 Hearing" sets their volume. Echo cancelling is on in a room; calls come back by themselves after a drop.

CHARACTERS > Look: "Light just on <puppet>": Off / Auto (brighter the darker the sky) / Soft / Bright front light plus a Rim light, lighting only that puppet, never the set. "Same look on all puppets" copies outline + light to everyone. The outline section is more compact.

Phone: the 3D view sits on top and every panel stacks underneath in one column you scroll with a finger. Taps press buttons when you lift without sliding; sliders still drag. "✋ View / 👆 Tool" picks what one finger does in 3D (two fingers always move the view), "⇕ Size" makes the 3D view bigger or smaller. Edit shows the film on top and the timeline scrolls sideways.

Blender export: puppet arms come in as curves that move every frame; outlines become a Solidify shell; a puppet's own light becomes linked lights (Blender light linking); glowing clay glows in its own colors. Phones and desktops in the room can now make the Blender zip too (they get the latest film first).

title: 10 new upbeat songs (dance, pop, funk, jazz, acid, action, race, anime, wonky), a mood filter on Music, and Edit sound options that no longer get cut off
notes: New songs: Disco Ball Dash and Neon Skate Rink (dance), Bubblegum Sunshine (pop), Strut Your Stuff (funk), Swing Swing Scoot (big-band jazz), Acid Gumball (squelchy 303), Rocket Rescue (action), Turbo Lap (race), Sparkle Opening (anime opening) and Wonky Washing Machine (wonky).
New instruments for them: acid bass, supersaw, synth bass, square lead, organ and sax.
Music page: mood buttons (All, Dance, Pop, Funk, Jazz, Acid, Action, Race, Anime, Wonky, Mellow). "All" lists the upbeat songs first and the slow ones last under Mellow.
Edit: with lots of camera lanes and sound lanes, tapping a sound lane now always shows its full options (effects row, split, word mutes); the sound lanes scroll with Up/Down to make room.

title: On a phone, exported videos go to Photos: tap "📲 Save to Photos", then "Save Video"
notes: After an export on a phone, a green "📲 Save to Photos" button shows in the top bar and on the Export page. It opens the share sheet; pick "Save Video" and it lands in the camera roll.
The button stays until you've saved (cancelling the sheet keeps it), so you can try again without exporting again.
"To Files" saves it to the Files app instead.
Before, a phone that wasn't joined to the headset tried to save by itself right after rendering, which iPhones block, so the video went nowhere.

title: Exported videos keep their sound on iPhone (AAC sound, checked before saving)
notes: The sound track is now made as AAC, which iPhone Photos plays. Before, if the phone's encoder said no to the first setting, the video could end up with sound that iPhones won't play, or none at all.
Every sound attempt is checked; if the phone's encoder can't make AAC, the phone records the film's mix as AAC in real time (takes as long as the film) instead.
Export page shows what the last video got: "with sound (AAC)" in green, or "NO SOUND" and why in red. The finished toast says it too.

title: Bendy sculpted arms, smooth joins when you redo part of a take, Music in EDIT, the mirror while wearing a puppet, and phone fixes
notes: Bendy arms (CHARACTERS > Puppet > Arms > Bendy, on by default): an arm you sculpt on a hand stays on at the shoulder, the hand end follows the hand, and the arm in between bends. Twisting your wrist no longer flings the whole arm around.

Smooth joins (PERFORM, next to "Hear old take while redoing"): when you redo part of an older take, the redo eases in from where everything was over ¼ s, and back out at the end. Tap for ½ s or hard joins.
EDIT now has a Music tab with every song and the mood buttons; the music lane's panel has "🎵 Pick another song".
Wearing a puppet with the mirror up shows you in the mirror even when the camera is on.
iPhone: sound plays in the app even with the ring switch on silent.
Phone export no longer reloads the page the first time: it draws the film with the same 3D engine instead of starting a second one.
Files: a world can no longer be listed twice (the second "(open)" was the same world listed twice).

title: Phone exports: the AAC sound is checked so iPhone Photos can play it
notes: iPhones hand back their AAC setup in a different wrapper than MP4 expects; a video with it plays silent. The setup is now unwrapped (or rebuilt) to the standard two bytes.
Before the sound goes in the video, the phone decodes the first second of it back. If that fails, it tries the next way of making the sound (another encoder setting, then real-time recording).
The Export page's "Last video" line now shows how the sound was made (for example "AAC · encoder · 1190"), to track down any phone that still comes out silent.

title: Bendy arms get two weights: how much of the arm stays with the shoulder and how much stays with the hand
notes: CHARACTERS > Puppet > Arms > tap "Bendy ▸": "Shoulder" sets how far down the arm stays put with the body (from your set shoulder point), "Hand" how much near the hand stays rigid with the hand. Everything in between bends softly. "Stiff" turns bending off.
Saved per puppet and shared with your partner.

title: The mirror shows just you, and your puppet's mouth moves with your voice while you try it on
notes: Mirror (wearing a puppet in CHARACTERS or PERFORM): only the puppet you're wearing, on a plain backdrop. No set, sky, water or other puppets.
Try it on: the mic turns on by itself, so the mouth follows your voice right away.
Voice page: while you try a voice with the mic on, the selected puppet's mouth moves too, even when you're not wearing it.

title: Stepping into a tilted or lying-down puppet works now: it stands up while you wear it and plays back tilted. Your left hand grabs and puppets too, so each hand can hold its own puppet, prop or eye target. A puppet you hold opens its mouth when you talk.
notes: Wearing a tilted puppet: it stands up straight where it lay (same spot, lowest point kept), you stay level and never tip. Your head and hand moves are kept relative to its body, so the take plays back tilted the way you placed it. Same when its recorded walk tips over.
Stepping out levels you again.
Left grip in Perform grabs a puppet, its eye target or a moving prop (left trigger re-grips). Both hands record at once.
Held puppet's mouth follows your mic, like wearing it.

title: Heads and bodies stay together across takes, Lights, Sun, Sky and Material now live in BUILD, and 8 new songs.
notes: Head and body: when takes recorded at different times (or a walk past the end of an older take) leave the body somewhere else, the body slides back under the head on playback. Close nods and leans stay as recorded. Riding a recorded walk now records the body following your head too.
BUILD rail: Sculpt, Doodle, Blocks, Color, Material, Lights, Sun, Sky, Layers. LIGHT is gone from the dial.

New songs: Key Change Carousel (climbs two keys), Seven-Eight Skate Sprint (7/8), Tritone Taxi (bebop with tritone subs), Popcorn Polyrhythm (3s and 5s over 4), Comet Kids (anime opening, key change), Samba Supernova (batucada), Acid Phase Drift (7- and 5-step acid lines), Boss Battle Hemiola (3/4 with hemiola and a Neapolitan chord).

title: You step into a tilted puppet at the angle you placed it, lists scroll everywhere and show how many are hidden, and worlds can be named and duplicated.
notes: Tilted puppet: you tip with it, so its down is your down. Walking with the stick follows its own ground. Stepping out levels you. Takes play back at the placed angle.

Lists: ▲n / ▼n show how many rows are hidden above and below, with a yellow drag bar and a yellow edge. Right stick (pointing at the list) or mouse wheel scrolls. Applies to Camera takes, Motion, Voices, On stage, Songs, Worlds, GitHub worlds, Other worlds, Prop from a layer, the Layers window and the Characters page.
Camera tab: every take, first on top; the picked one has Path, Keys and delete buttons. Path and Keys have a back button.

Files: this world's name (tap to rename), Duplicate, and the whole world list. New worlds and first saves ask for a name.

title: Sliding a cut keeps the take you picked, mute just the sound between two cuts, a taller editor, one character list and one library for all worlds, outside-only outlines, and "Turn any way" holds the world in one hand.
notes: Edit: sliding the white join between two clips no longer makes a stray yellow ✕ cut or loses the take you chose. Tap a sound block between two cuts, then "Mute between cuts". New buttons: ↕ Short/Tall/Taller window, 🎞 rows S/M/L, ♪ rows S/M/L. Hidden sound lanes show "▲ 2 more / ▼ 1 more".

Characters: new "All" tab lists every character with rename, copy and delete. Library shows every character from every other world in one grid. On stage (ACTION) has Delete and All characters. The Delete row on the Puppet page can no longer fall off the bottom.

Look: outline "Outside only" traces just the whole puppet against the background; thickness is a slider down to a hairline.
Turn any way: one grip moves and turns the world exactly with that hand; two grips also size you.
Doodles remember which way was up when you drew them. Layers window: "Doodles: my down" / "World down". A doodle you turn by hand stays the way you put it down. Sky page: "Sky down = my down".
Sock puppets: only the front of the mouth opens, so nothing pokes out the back of the head; the sleeve bends down at the wrist like a forearm.
Camera lens zoom on the stick is faster.

title: CHARACTERS and EDIT always keep the ground down, even with "Turn any way" on. Your turned view of the world comes back when you return to BUILD or ACTION.
notes: CHARACTERS and EDIT always keep the ground down, even with "Turn any way" on. Your turned view of the world comes back when you return to BUILD or ACTION.
